candidate.name: Basepilot
candidate.long_description:
Basepilot helps insurers, TPAs and MGAs streamline claims operations with line-of-business-specific AI agents. Companies like Old Republic International, Zurich & others use Basepilot to make claims operations more efficient, less costly and more intelligent.

Basepilot is founded by Ken Hendricks and Pascal Wieler.

Interested to try it out? Get started here: https://www.basepilot.com/

founders.name: Ken Hendricks
founders.title: Founder/CEO
founders.bio:
I’m Ken, co-founder and CEO of Basepilot. We build AI coworkers that collaborate with humans to automate work. 

Prior to Basepilot, I led product at a B2B fintech startup and grew it to 3M users in <12 months, with customers like Visa and Bank of America. Before that, I built a computer vision startup out of university that reached $250K ARR with partnerships like Deloitte, KPMG, EY and BMW. 

Born in Mumbai, brought up in New Zealand, before moving to SF. Studied Mechatronics eng.

founders.name: Pascal Wieler
founders.title: Founder/CTO
founders.bio:
Hi! I'm Pascal, Co-founder of Basepilot. I grew up in Germany.

Passionate about AI agents, robotics & outdoor sports 🤖🚵. Studied CS MSc. @CMU MLD & KIT. Previously, I co-founded a robotics startup, did research in robotic manipulation & imitation learning at Carnegie Mellon, and worked on self-driving cars at Mercedes-Benz. Excited to be a part of YC, let's chat!

score.thesis: AI-native autonomous agents owning high-value business workflows

analysis.team: Two-person founding team with strong technical and startup pedigree. Ken Hendricks (CEO) previously led product at a B2B fintech that grew to 3M users in under 12 months with customers like Visa and Bank of America, and earlier built a computer vision startup to $250K ARR with partners including Deloitte, KPMG, EY and BMW (Founder bio: Ken Hendricks). Pascal Wieler (CTO) holds a CS MSc from CMU MLD and KIT, co-founded a robotics startup, did research in robotic manipulation and imitation learning at Carnegie Mellon, and worked on self-driving cars at Mercedes-Benz (Founder bio: Pascal Wieler). The team blends product/commercial experience with deep AI/ML research depth.
analysis.product: Basepilot builds line-of-business-specific AI agents for insurance claims operations, targeting insurers, TPAs and MGAs to make claims processing more efficient, less costly and more intelligent (YC long description, One-liner). The founders describe the product as 'AI coworkers that collaborate with humans to automate work' (Founder bio: Ken Hendricks). YC tags include AI Assistant, No-code and Automation, suggesting a human-in-the-loop assistive framing rather than fully autonomous execution (YC industries/tags).
analysis.market: The target market is insurance claims operations serving insurers, TPAs and MGAs (YC long description). The sources name Old Republic International and Zurich among customers using Basepilot (YC long description). No market size, TAM, revenue, pricing, or competitive landscape is provided in the sources — these are unknown. A specific 'why-now' is not stated beyond the general availability of AI agents; treat the timing thesis as unverified.
risks: Workflow framing is mixed: YC tags 'AI Assistant' and the founders describe 'AI coworkers that collaborate with humans,' suggesting an assistive tool rather than an agent that autonomously owns the claims workflow (YC industries/tags; Founder bio: Ken Hendricks).
No explicit autonomy language in the sources — unclear how much of the claims workflow the agents actually execute end-to-end versus assist (Score breakdown: Autonomy 0/15).

Company is tiny (team size 2) and no momentum signals (hiring, traction metrics, revenue) are available; depth of the named Old Republic/Zurich relationships is unspecified (YC team size; YC long description).
Insurance claims is a regulated, incumbent-heavy domain; competitive landscape and defensibility are entirely absent from the sources.
what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that Basepilot's agents autonomously own and execute a high-value claims workflow end-to-end (e.g. adjudication or settlement) rather than assisting humans.
Traction proof from the named customers — production deployments, contract value, or volume of claims processed at Old Republic International and Zurich (YC long description).
Momentum signals such as active hiring, revenue growth, or expansion beyond claims into broader autonomous operations.
analysis.recommendation_rationale: Pass, consistent with the 28/100 weak score. Despite a strong, technically deep founding team (10/10), the product is framed as an AI assistant / coworker collaborating with humans rather than an autonomous agent owning a high-value workflow, scoring zero on both workflow ownership and autonomy — the core of the thesis (Score breakdown; Founder bio: Ken Hendricks; YC industries/tags). With no momentum data and only limited freshness credit, the venture does not currently fit the autonomous-agent thesis, though evidence of true end-to-end autonomy could warrant a re-look.
